title: Universality and ambiguity in extremes of anomalous diffusion
summary: Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models, (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows, and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffusive search compared to normal diffusion. Though mathematically rigorous, the relevance of (i) and (ii) to actual physical systems is suspect since their derivations involve searchers which move with unbounded speed.
